t: What Are In The Money Options ( ITM Options )? by www.OptionTradingpedia.com
s: A call option is considered In The Money ( ITM ) when the call option's strike price is lower than the prevailing market price of the underlying stock, thus allowing its owner to buy the underlying stock at lower than the prevailing market price by exercising the call option.

t: Pros and Cons of In- and Out-of-the-Money Options | Nasdaq
s: So, if shares of XYZ are trading at $40, the February 50 put will be ITM. Conversely, a February 30 put would be OTM, if XYZ is trading at $40. Like all trades, in-the-money options have risks and rewards. These options are generally viewed as the more "conservative" choice, as they have higher deltas -- the measure of how much an options price will change based on the movement of an underlying stock -- meaning there's a better chance for the option to be in-the-money at the time of expiration. Buying ITM options also lessens the impact of time decay, as they carry both intrinsic and time value.
